summary: 40-foot L-5 lookout on Rujada Point, Lane County, OR, completed 1934; removed about 1960 or destroyed (sources differ); no site description found.

facts.status_note: Removed about 1960 per one source; other sources say abandoned and destroyed

events.note: The Sentinel item dated August 11, 1933: material arrived and work was to start; timber felled to improve visibility
Roseburg Chieftain item dated September 14, 1933: CCC to build a 10x10 lookout before the first snow; 10x10 called the standard size for secondary lookouts
40-foot round fir pole tower with a 10x10 L-5 cab completed
About 1960 per the Oregon lookouts page; the register says abandoned and removed, firelookout.com says abandoned and destroyed (no year given)

evidence.supports: 40-foot L-5 tower built in 1934, later abandoned and removed
evidence.quote: This 40' wooden L-5 tower, built in 1934 atop a minor summit one mile west northwest of Rose Hill, was later abandoned and removed.

evidence.supports: tower abandoned and destroyed (conflicts with removal)
evidence.quote: This 40' wooden L-5 tower, built in 1934, was later abandoned and destroyed.

notes_for_editor: Three pages read; no staffing, fire or access record found, so none written. Access and visit keys omitted (brief says unknown and no source gives one). Sources disagree on removal (removed about 1960 vs destroyed, undated). The 1933 Sentinel and Roseburg Chieftain items are only seen as quoted on the Oregon lookouts page. Lead, not used: a Dorena Historical Society Facebook post (Curtis Irish archive) shows the Rujada tower in 1940; the page would not load (login wall), so it is not cited. Brief record checked: L-5, 40 ft/12.2 m, Umpqua NF and 2011 registration all agree with sources; no corrections.
